newsitem.title: FRANCE: FORECAST - Analysts mixed on Alcatel H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Analysts mixed on Alcatel H1.

text.p: If there is one thing about Alcatel Alsthom's first half results, due on Thursday, that financial analysts agree about then it is that they are very difficult to call.
On a pure headline figure basis, Alcatel is seen posting a net attributable loss of between 500 million francs and 1.5 billion francs. A big range reflecting the uncertainty.
In last year's first half results, the first set of figures announced by then freshly-appointed chairman Serge Tchuruk ahead of his restructuring plans, the group lost 1.231 billion francs.

At the full-year stage, most analysts expect a return to the black with a 1996 profit figure of over one billion francs, against a loss of 25.6 billion francs, the biggest loss in French corporate history.
According to research specialist Jacques Chahine Finance, a poll of 28 analysts conducted on September 20 found an average earnings per share figure of 10.6 francs for 1996.
The range is from a loss of two francs to a profit of 24.7 francs per share.
"In fact, the headline figure is meaningless as there are so many factors that could influence it," an analyst said.

"For me, the only really important figure is the operating income for the telecoms sector which I see at a loss of one billion francs," added the analyst at a big brokerage in London, known to be a bear on Alcatel.

"I agree that the telecoms operating losses will be the swing factor. We don't have a half year forecast because the company usually does not provide this at the half year stage," said another analyst who can be placed among the Alcatel bulls.
"We see a half year loss of 540 million francs and a full year profit of 1.28 billion," she added. First half sales were down 1.5 pct to 74.3 billion, with a rise in telecoms.
Ian Macleod at Natwest Sellier in Paris said he expected half a billion francs in first half losses.

Alcatel's telecommunications division is key for the group's results. In the past year, mounting losses at this division's German, Spanish and Turkish units as well as declining margins in France were the main reason behind Alcatel's loss.

But the historic loss figure of 25.6 billion francs was reached after non-recurring charges of 23.9 billion francs of which 21.6 billion were for provisions and write-downs as part of a far-reaching restructuring programme.
Tchuruk has broken up the telecommunications division's country-based organisation and put in place a product and client-type structure instead.
For analysts, the big question is whether the first benefits on the results from this restructuring will already be visible.
Big question marks also hang over the amount of tax losses Alcatel can use to reduce its tax bill and the asset gains to be booked in the first half.
A few hundred million francs in asset gains are expected in the first half, on operations such as the sale of a two percent Fiat stake for 350 billion lire.

The big ticket operation for 1996 asset gains will be the sale of Alcatel's 20 percent stake in Cie Generale des Eaux's Cofira mobile telecoms holding, expected in the second half of the year. Alcatel has announced the sale but the timing is open.

Another item that will have big consequences on the net figure will be the amount of goodwill amortisation Alcatel will make, with analysts' full year estimates ranging from one billion to 2.8 billion francs.
To top all that, the Alcatel Alsthom that will present its first half results on Thursday will have completely changed at the end-year stage.

At that time, it will own more than half of the GEC-Alsthom NV joint venture with GEC Plc which will have absorbed AEG's T&D unit and state-owned nuclear engineering group Framatome. It is now a 50/50 venture.
Alcatel may have acquired Thomson SA from the state and could perhaps have completed finding allies for the consumer to defence electronics group.
"We don't know exactly where Alcatel is going but we have a good feel about it. But to be honest, the Thomson announcement was a big surprise and raised many questions," an analyst said.
"The share came down from some 500 francs to 390 now. We had a price target of 550 francs but Thomson put the share off course," she added.
